<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-this-evidence-show-that-organic-leafy-greens-are-cleaner" data-anchor="does-this-evidence-show-that-organic-leafy-greens-are-cleaner" data-question="Does this evidence show that organic leafy greens are cleaner?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does this evidence show that organic leafy greens are cleaner?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Not consistently. In a long-term English trial, organic crop protection changed only cabbage nickel, while farmyard manure lowered cadmium; in New Zealand, organic market-garden vegetables were lower in cadmium and nickel overall but not consistently by leaf.<sup class="cite">[[sources/rempelos2023-vegetable-organic-conventional-metals|19]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Leonidas Rempelos, Marcin Baranski, Enas Khalid Sufar, Jenny Gilroy, Peter Shotton, Halima Leifert, Dominika Srednicka-Tober, Gultekin Hasanaliyeva, Eduardo A. S. Rosa, Jana Hajslova, Vera Schulzova, Ismail Cakmak, Levent Ozturk, Kirsten Brandt, Chris Seal, Juan Wang, Christoph Schmidt, Carlo Leifert · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rempelos2023-vegetable-organic-conventional-metals">Effect of Climatic Conditions, and Agronomic Practices Used in Organic and Conventional Crop Production on Yield and Nutritional Composition Parameters in Potato, Cabbage, Lettuce and Onion; Results from the Long-Term NFSC-Trials</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Agronomy</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rempelos2023-vegetable-organic-conventional-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/dearing2025-nz-organic-nonorganic-vegetables-cyclone|33]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Dearing C, Ye Z, Robertshaw G · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/dearing2025-nz-organic-nonorganic-vegetables-cyclone">Assessment of Heavy Metals in Organic and Non-Organic Vegetables Post Severe Tropical Cyclone Gabrielle: A cross-sectional comparative analysis</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">F1000Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/dearing2025-nz-organic-nonorganic-vegetables-cyclone">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Manures raised lead in Turkish spinach, so an organic label alone does not establish lower metals.<sup class="cite">[[sources/authors2022-compared-to-the-chemical-fertilizer-in-organic-fertilizer|21]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Unknown authors · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/authors2022-compared-to-the-chemical-fertilizer-in-organic-fertilizer">compared to the chemical fertilizer. In organic fertilizer applications, heavy metal contents such as arsenic, chrome, cobalt, and nickel were found to</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Peer-reviewed article</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/authors2022-compared-to-the-chemical-fertilizer-in-organic-fertilizer">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-leafy-greens-have-the-lowest-cadmium" data-anchor="which-leafy-greens-have-the-lowest-cadmium" data-question="Which leafy greens have the lowest cadmium?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which leafy greens have the lowest cadmium?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Head cabbage, followed by head and iceberg lettuce; lamb’s lettuce and watercress were also low where measured.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements|15]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Veronica Martin-Leon, Carmen Rubio, Angel Rodriguez-Hernandez, Manuel Zumbado, Andrea Acosta-Dacal, Luis Alberto Henriquez-Hernandez, Luis D. Boada, Maria del Mar Travieso-Aja, Octavio P. Luzardo · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements">Evaluation of essential, toxic and potentially toxic elements in leafy vegetables grown in the Canary Islands</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxics</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Spinach was highest in every large dataset, with a GEMS/Food median of about 41 µg/kg against 2–4 µg/kg for cabbage.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-leafy-greens-have-the-lowest-lead" data-anchor="which-leafy-greens-have-the-lowest-lead" data-question="Which leafy greens have the lowest lead?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which leafy greens have the lowest lead?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Iceberg lettuce and cabbage in monitored markets: FDA detected lead in none of 27 composites of either, and iceberg had the lowest lead median (2.0 µg/kg) in Gran Canaria.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements|15]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Veronica Martin-Leon, Carmen Rubio, Angel Rodriguez-Hernandez, Manuel Zumbado, Andrea Acosta-Dacal, Luis Alberto Henriquez-Hernandez, Luis D. Boada, Maria del Mar Travieso-Aja, Octavio P. Luzardo · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements">Evaluation of essential, toxic and potentially toxic elements in leafy vegetables grown in the Canary Islands</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxics</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Kale, spinach and lamb’s lettuce had higher lead medians (13–25 µg/kg) in GEMS/Food.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-leafy-vegetables-had-the-lowest-measured-aluminium" data-anchor="which-leafy-vegetables-had-the-lowest-measured-aluminium" data-question="Which leafy vegetables had the lowest measured aluminium?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which leafy vegetables had the lowest measured aluminium?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Iceberg lettuce (1,581 µg/kg) in Gran Canaria and Chinese cabbage (200 µg/kg) in Hong Kong; spinach and Chinese spinach were highest.<sup class="cite">[[sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements|15]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Veronica Martin-Leon, Carmen Rubio, Angel Rodriguez-Hernandez, Manuel Zumbado, Andrea Acosta-Dacal, Luis Alberto Henriquez-Hernandez, Luis D. Boada, Maria del Mar Travieso-Aja, Octavio P. Luzardo · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements">Evaluation of essential, toxic and potentially toxic elements in leafy vegetables grown in the Canary Islands</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxics</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants|16]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Centre for Food Safety (Hong Kong) · 2013</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants">The First Hong Kong Total Diet Study: Metallic Contaminants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Centre for Food Safety, Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cfs2013-hktds-metallic-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Aluminium varies more than twenty-fold between leaves in the same survey, so leaf type matters more than origin.<sup class="cite">[[sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements|15]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Veronica Martin-Leon, Carmen Rubio, Angel Rodriguez-Hernandez, Manuel Zumbado, Andrea Acosta-Dacal, Luis Alberto Henriquez-Hernandez, Luis D. Boada, Maria del Mar Travieso-Aja, Octavio P. Luzardo · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements">Evaluation of essential, toxic and potentially toxic elements in leafy vegetables grown in the Canary Islands</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxics</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="which-growing-country-has-the-lowest-heavy-metal-levels" data-anchor="which-growing-country-has-the-lowest-heavy-metal-levels" data-question="Which growing country has the lowest heavy metal levels?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Which growing country has the lowest heavy metal levels?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

No country ranking is supported. GEMS/Food reports reporting regions rather than growing countries: lead was higher in Western Pacific submissions from 2001–2009 and cadmium in spinach higher in the Americas than in Europe, but these regions cover different years.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The clearest lower-contamination origin is a growing site away from mining, industry, roads and contaminated water.<sup class="cite">[[sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Li R, Wu H, Ding J, Fu W, Gan L, Li Y · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains">Mercury pollution in vegetables, grains and soils from areas surrounding coal-fired power plants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/rossini-oliva2024-urban-garden-vegetables-spain|10]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Rossini-Oliva S, López Nuñez R · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/rossini-oliva2024-urban-garden-vegetables-spain">Is it healthy urban agriculture? Human exposure to potentially toxic elements in urban gardens from Andalusia, Spain</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Environmental Science and Pollution Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/rossini-oliva2024-urban-garden-vegetables-spain">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/kim2024-metals-kale-urban-rural-maryland|17]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Kim BF, Lupolt SN, Santo RE, Bachman G, Zhu X, Yang T, Fukagawa NK, Richardson ML, Green C, Phillips KM, Nachman KE · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kim2024-metals-kale-urban-rural-maryland">Nutrients and non-essential metals in darkibor kale grown at urban and rural farms: a pilot study</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">PLOS ONE</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kim2024-metals-kale-urban-rural-maryland">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="do-these-measurements-predict-my-personal-health-risk" data-anchor="do-these-measurements-predict-my-personal-health-risk" data-question="Do these measurements predict my personal health risk?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Do these measurements predict my personal health risk?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

No. They describe concentrations; risk depends on how much you eat, your other diet and your health.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2012-cadmium-dietary-exposure-europe|39]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2012-cadmium-dietary-exposure-europe">Cadmium dietary exposure in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2012;10(1):2551</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2012-cadmium-dietary-exposure-europe">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/masri2025-toxicant-foods-california|43]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Masri S, Nasla S, Payán DD, Wu J · 2025</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/masri2025-toxicant-foods-california">Assessing Dietary Consumption of Toxicant-Laden Foods and Beverages by Age and Ethnicity in California: Implications for Proposition 65</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Nutrients</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/masri2025-toxicant-foods-california">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In Europe leafy vegetables supplied about 4–6% of adult cadmium exposure.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2012-cadmium-dietary-exposure-europe|39]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2012-cadmium-dietary-exposure-europe">Cadmium dietary exposure in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2012;10(1):2551</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2012-cadmium-dietary-exposure-europe">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-washing-remove-every-metal-from-leafy-greens" data-anchor="does-washing-remove-every-metal-from-leafy-greens" data-question="Does washing remove every metal from leafy greens?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does washing remove every metal from leafy greens?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

No. Washing removed most surface cadmium, nickel and mercury in roadside and power-plant studies, but a vinegar soak left lead in farm lettuce unchanged, because metal taken up into the leaf stays.<sup class="cite">[[sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains|6]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Li R, Wu H, Ding J, Fu W, Gan L, Li Y · 2017</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains">Mercury pollution in vegetables, grains and soils from areas surrounding coal-fired power plants</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Scientific Reports</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/li2017-mercury-coal-power-plants-vegetables-grains">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/adhikari2024-leafy-vegetables-johannesburg|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Adhikari S, Struwig M · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/adhikari2024-leafy-vegetables-johannesburg">Concentrations and health risks of selected elements in leafy vegetables: a comparison between roadside open-air markets and large stores in Johannesburg, South Africa</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Not reported</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/adhikari2024-leafy-vegetables-johannesburg">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/bora2022-heavy-metals-fruits-vegetables-romania-vinegar-washing|25]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Bora FD, Bunea A, Pop SR, Banita SI, Dusa DS, Chira A, Bunea CI · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bora2022-heavy-metals-fruits-vegetables-romania-vinegar-washing">Quantification and Reduction in Heavy Metal Residues in Some Fruits and Vegetables: A Case Study Galați County, Romania</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Horticulturae</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bora2022-heavy-metals-fruits-vegetables-romania-vinegar-washing">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="is-total-arsenic-the-same-as-inorganic-arsenic" data-anchor="is-total-arsenic-the-same-as-inorganic-arsenic" data-question="Is total arsenic the same as inorganic arsenic?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Is total arsenic the same as inorganic arsenic?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

No. Inorganic arsenic is the more toxic part; Hong Kong measured it directly and found 74 µg/kg in water spinach but none detected in European cabbage or lettuce.<sup class="cite">[[sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Centre for Food Safety FEHD HKSAR · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic">The First Hong Kong Total Diet Study: Inorganic Arsenic</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Centre for Food Safety, Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Most surveys report total arsenic only.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements|15]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Veronica Martin-Leon, Carmen Rubio, Angel Rodriguez-Hernandez, Manuel Zumbado, Andrea Acosta-Dacal, Luis Alberto Henriquez-Hernandez, Luis D. Boada, Maria del Mar Travieso-Aja, Octavio P. Luzardo · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements">Evaluation of essential, toxic and potentially toxic elements in leafy vegetables grown in the Canary Islands</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Toxics</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/martin-leon2023-canary-leafy-vegetables-elements">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-soaking-overnight-reduce-metals" data-anchor="does-soaking-overnight-reduce-metals" data-question="Does soaking overnight reduce metals?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does soaking overnight reduce metals?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

No study in the library tested an overnight water soak. A 5–10 minute vinegar soak lowered surface lead in market lettuce, and boiling in clean water removed part of the arsenic from amaranth.<sup class="cite">[[sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Clair-Caliot G, Marks SJ, Hug SJ, Bretzler A, N&#39;guessan ND, Tihe SFK, Lalanne F · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina">Uptake of Arsenic by Irrigated Vegetables and Cooked Food Products in Burkina Faso</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Water</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/bora2022-heavy-metals-fruits-vegetables-romania-vinegar-washing|25]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Bora FD, Bunea A, Pop SR, Banita SI, Dusa DS, Chira A, Bunea CI · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/bora2022-heavy-metals-fruits-vegetables-romania-vinegar-washing">Quantification and Reduction in Heavy Metal Residues in Some Fruits and Vegetables: A Case Study Galați County, Romania</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Horticulturae</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/bora2022-heavy-metals-fruits-vegetables-romania-vinegar-washing">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="can-non-detects-identify-the-cleanest-type" data-anchor="can-non-detects-identify-the-cleanest-type" data-question="Can non-detects identify the cleanest type?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Can non-detects identify the cleanest type?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Only when the detection limits are low enough.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> A result below a 4 µg/kg limit says more than one below 200 µg/kg, and non-detects with different limits cannot be ranked against each other.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-a-supermarket-guarantee-lower-levels" data-anchor="does-a-supermarket-guarantee-lower-levels" data-question="Does a supermarket guarantee lower levels?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does a supermarket guarantee lower levels?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

No, though supermarket leaves were lower than roadside leaves in Johannesburg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/adhikari2024-leafy-vegetables-johannesburg|7]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Adhikari S, Struwig M · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/adhikari2024-leafy-vegetables-johannesburg">Concentrations and health risks of selected elements in leafy vegetables: a comparison between roadside open-air markets and large stores in Johannesburg, South Africa</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Not reported</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/adhikari2024-leafy-vegetables-johannesburg">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Supermarket monitoring datasets still include spinach and lettuce results above EU cadmium limits.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa-cadmium-contam-2009|4]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">EFSA Panel on Contaminants in the Food Chain (CONTAM) · 2009</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa-cadmium-contam-2009">Scientific Opinion of the Panel on Contaminants in the Food Chain on a request from the European Commission on cadmium in food</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">The EFSA Journal</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa-cadmium-contam-2009">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="why-are-dry-weight-results-different-from-fresh-weight-results" data-anchor="why-are-dry-weight-results-different-from-fresh-weight-results" data-question="Why are dry-weight results different from fresh-weight results?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Why are dry-weight results different from fresh-weight results?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Because fresh leaves are about 90% water.<sup class="cite">[[sources/cherfi2014-algeria-fruits-vegetables-metals|11]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Cherfi A, Abdoun S, Gaci O · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cherfi2014-algeria-fruits-vegetables-metals">Food survey: Levels and potential health risks of chromium, lead, zinc and copper content in fruits and vegetables consumed in Algeria</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food and Chemical Toxicology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cherfi2014-algeria-fruits-vegetables-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Removing the water concentrates the metal, so a dry-weight result is roughly ten times the fresh-weight value; limits are set on fresh weight.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/cherfi2014-algeria-fruits-vegetables-metals|11]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Cherfi A, Abdoun S, Gaci O · 2014</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cherfi2014-algeria-fruits-vegetables-metals">Food survey: Levels and potential health risks of chromium, lead, zinc and copper content in fruits and vegetables consumed in Algeria</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Food and Chemical Toxicology</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cherfi2014-algeria-fruits-vegetables-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-cooking-reduce-metals-in-leafy-greens" data-anchor="does-cooking-reduce-metals-in-leafy-greens" data-question="Does cooking reduce metals in leafy greens?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does cooking reduce metals in leafy greens?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Sometimes, and it depends on the metal and leaf.<sup class="cite">[[sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Clair-Caliot G, Marks SJ, Hug SJ, Bretzler A, N&#39;guessan ND, Tihe SFK, Lalanne F · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina">Uptake of Arsenic by Irrigated Vegetables and Cooked Food Products in Burkina Faso</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Water</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/kananke2026-sri-lanka-leaf-bioaccessibility|26]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Thilini Kananke, Jagath Wansapala, Anil Gunarathne · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kananke2026-sri-lanka-leaf-bioaccessibility">Bioaccessibility of Heavy Metals in Raw and Processed Alternanthera sessilis and Centella asiatica: An In vitro Study</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Nature Environment and Pollution Technology25(1):D1830</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kananke2026-sri-lanka-leaf-bioaccessibility">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Boiling removed 55–69% of arsenic from amaranth but only 3–31% from spinach, and cooking with coconut milk or oil generally lowered the bioaccessible fraction of several metals.<sup class="cite">[[sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Clair-Caliot G, Marks SJ, Hug SJ, Bretzler A, N&#39;guessan ND, Tihe SFK, Lalanne F · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina">Uptake of Arsenic by Irrigated Vegetables and Cooked Food Products in Burkina Faso</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Water</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/kananke2026-sri-lanka-leaf-bioaccessibility|26]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Thilini Kananke, Jagath Wansapala, Anil Gunarathne · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/kananke2026-sri-lanka-leaf-bioaccessibility">Bioaccessibility of Heavy Metals in Raw and Processed Alternanthera sessilis and Centella asiatica: An In vitro Study</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Nature Environment and Pollution Technology25(1):D1830</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/kananke2026-sri-lanka-leaf-bioaccessibility">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="are-there-legal-limits-for-heavy-metals-in-leafy-greens" data-anchor="are-there-legal-limits-for-heavy-metals-in-leafy-greens" data-question="Are there legal limits for heavy metals in leafy greens?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Are there legal limits for heavy metals in leafy greens?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Yes: the EU sets 0.30 mg/kg lead and 0.10 mg/kg cadmium (0.20 mg/kg for spinach and fresh herbs), Codex 0.3 mg/kg lead and 0.2 mg/kg cadmium, and China 0.3 and 0.2 mg/kg.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/codex-cxs-193-1995|34]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Codex Alimentarius Commission · 1995</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">General Standard for Contaminants and Toxins in Food and Feed (CXS 193-1995)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Codex Alimentarius (Joint FAO/WHO Food Standards Programme)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/codex-cxs-193-1995">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/usda-fas2023-china-gb-2762-2022-translation|35]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">USDA Foreign Agricultural Service, FAS China Staff (Beijing) · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/usda-fas2023-china-gb-2762-2022-translation">China Releases the Standard for Maximum Levels of Contaminants in Foods (USDA FAS GAIN Report CH2023-0040, unofficial translation of GB 2762-2022)</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">USDA Foreign Agricultural Service, Global Agricultural Information Network (GAIN), Report Number CH2023-0040</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/usda-fas2023-china-gb-2762-2022-translation">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> The EU also sets 0.50 mg/kg nickel for leafy vegetables from 1 July 2025.<sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels|36]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2024</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2024/1987 of 30 July 2024 amending Regulation (EU) 2023/915 as regards maximum levels of nickel in certain foodstuffs</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union, L series, 2024/1987 (31.7.2024)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2024-1987-nickel-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="does-wastewater-irrigation-raise-metals-in-leafy-greens" data-anchor="does-wastewater-irrigation-raise-metals-in-leafy-greens" data-question="Does wastewater irrigation raise metals in leafy greens?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Does wastewater irrigation raise metals in leafy greens?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

Yes, in the field studies that compared it.<sup class="cite">[[sources/naser2018-leafy-vegetables-bangladesh-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Naser HM, Rahman MZ, Sultana S, Quddus MA, Hossain MA · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/naser2018-leafy-vegetables-bangladesh-metals">Heavy metal accumulation in leafy vegetables grown in industrial areas under varying levels of pollution</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bangladesh Journal of Agricultural Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/naser2018-leafy-vegetables-bangladesh-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Clair-Caliot G, Marks SJ, Hug SJ, Bretzler A, N&#39;guessan ND, Tihe SFK, Lalanne F · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina">Uptake of Arsenic by Irrigated Vegetables and Cooked Food Products in Burkina Faso</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Water</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> Leaves near industrial effluent in Bangladesh carried several times the lead and cadmium of leaves from a low-pollution field, and arsenic in irrigation water raised leaf arsenic in proportion.<sup class="cite">[[sources/naser2018-leafy-vegetables-bangladesh-metals|3]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Naser HM, Rahman MZ, Sultana S, Quddus MA, Hossain MA · 2018</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/naser2018-leafy-vegetables-bangladesh-metals">Heavy metal accumulation in leafy vegetables grown in industrial areas under varying levels of pollution</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Bangladesh Journal of Agricultural Research</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/naser2018-leafy-vegetables-bangladesh-metals">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina|14]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Clair-Caliot G, Marks SJ, Hug SJ, Bretzler A, N&#39;guessan ND, Tihe SFK, Lalanne F · 2021</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina">Uptake of Arsenic by Irrigated Vegetables and Cooked Food Products in Burkina Faso</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Frontiers in Water</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/clair-caliot2021-arsenic-irrigated-vegetables-burkina">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="what-should-a-supplier-laboratory-report-identify" data-anchor="what-should-a-supplier-laboratory-report-identify" data-question="What should a supplier laboratory report identify?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>What should a supplier laboratory report identify?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

The leaf, the edible part analysed, whether it was washed, the fresh-weight basis, the quantification limit for each metal and the growing site.<sup class="cite">[[sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020|2]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">U.S. Food and Drug Administration · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">FY2018-FY2020 TDS Elements Analytical Results</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">FDA Total Diet Study</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/fda2022-tds-elements-fy2018-fy2020">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels|8]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Commission · 2023</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Commission Regulation (EU) 2023/915 of 25 April 2023 on maximum levels for certain contaminants in food and repealing Regulation (EC) No 1881/2006</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Official Journal of the European Union</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/eu-2023-915-contaminants-maximum-levels">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> For arsenic and mercury it should say whether totals or species were measured.<sup class="cite">[[sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants|1]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">World Health Organization · 2026</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">GEMS/Food Contaminants database heavy-metal exports</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">GEMS/Food Contamination Monitoring and Assessment Programme</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/who-gemsfood-heavy-metal-contaminants">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic|5]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Centre for Food Safety FEHD HKSAR · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic">The First Hong Kong Total Diet Study: Inorganic Arsenic</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">Centre for Food Safety, Food and Environmental Hygiene Department, Government of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/cfs2012-hktds-inorganic-arsenic">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>

<details class="qa" data-hmi-faq="1" id="are-leafy-greens-a-major-source-of-cadmium-in-the-diet" data-anchor="are-leafy-greens-a-major-source-of-cadmium-in-the-diet" data-question="Are leafy greens a major source of cadmium in the diet?">
<summary><span class="mk" aria-hidden="true"></span>Are leafy greens a major source of cadmium in the diet?</summary>
<div class="ans" data-hmi-faq-answer="1">

A modest one.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2012-cadmium-dietary-exposure-europe|39]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2012-cadmium-dietary-exposure-europe">Cadmium dietary exposure in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2012;10(1):2551</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2012-cadmium-dietary-exposure-europe">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022|40]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022">Cadmium: dietary exposure assessment</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">WHO Food Additives Series, No. 82 (Safety evaluation of certain contaminants in food, prepared by the 91st meeting of JECFA)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022">Read source →</a></span></span></sup> In Europe they supplied 3.9% of cadmium exposure overall; national estimates cited by JECFA are 11% in China and 20% in the USA.<sup class="cite">[[sources/efsa2012-cadmium-dietary-exposure-europe|39]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">European Food Safety Authority · 2012</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/efsa2012-cadmium-dietary-exposure-europe">Cadmium dietary exposure in the European population</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">EFSA Journal 2012;10(1):2551</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/efsa2012-cadmium-dietary-exposure-europe">Read source →</a></span></span></sup><sup class="cite">[[sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022|40]]<span class="cite-card"><span class="cite-card-head"><span class="cite-card-authors">Joint FAO/WHO Expert Committee on Food Additives · 2022</span><a class="cite-card-title" href="../sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022">Cadmium: dietary exposure assessment</a></span><span class="cite-card-body"><span class="cite-card-journal">WHO Food Additives Series, No. 82 (Safety evaluation of certain contaminants in food, prepared by the 91st meeting of JECFA)</span><a class="cite-card-review" href="../sources/jecfa-91st-cadmium-2022">Read source →</a></span></span></sup>

</div>
</details>
